## Step 1 (build-time guardrail) in PR #3192

Shipping the **advisory build warning** first — it turns the silent runtime miss into a loud, self-correcting build signal without any runtime-behavior risk. `validateExpression` now flags `<dateField> ==/!= today()/daysFromNow()/daysAgo()/now()` and points at the working idioms; the stack linter threads each object's `date` field names in so it fires across formulas, validation, flow/action/sharing/hook predicates.

## Design note for the runtime fix (why "just hydrate date fields to `Date`" isn't enough)

Verified empirically in the formula engine:

| record field | `field == today()` | `field == "2026-06-20"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| string `"2026-06-20"` (today) | **false** ❌ | true ✅ |
| `Date` (UTC-midnight) | true ✅ | **false** ❌ |

So hydrating a `date` field to a `Date` at the data layer fixes `== today()` but **breaks `== "literal"`** — trading one silent-miss for another. A correct runtime fix must normalize by the *presence of a temporal operand* (e.g. AST-coerce the peer of a temporal function / date-literal comparison), not blanket-hydrate the field — and it has to cover every CEL site (`applyFormulaPlan` only sees `{name, expression}` + rows, no field types), so it's genuinely cross-cutting. Keeping this issue open for that design.
